newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac criticises French plan to restrict layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Chirac criticises French plan to restrict layoffs.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac criticised on Monday the left-wing government's plans to restore administrative restrictions on layoffs by private companies, saying it was an outdated idea.

In a live television interview, the conservative president said: "This debate is from another age...Today if we want to have a prosperous economy, employment and adapt to a changing world...we can no longer imprison the activities of those who create, invest and work in totally obsolete asd absurd regulations."

He was referring to plans announced by Socialist Labour Minister Martine Aubry to restore the requirement for state labour inspectors to approve all layoff plans, abolished by a right-wing government in 1986.

Chirac said he was in favour of defending a European social model and did not favour going as far as Britain or the United States in liberalising labour markets and withdrawing social protection for workers.
But he said France could not shackle its industrialists or shut itself off from alliances with European partners, saying it needed much greater freedom if it wanted economic growth.

The president also criticised the government's decision to shut down the Superphenix experimental nuclear fast-breeder reactor, noting that a broad consensus of French economic and social experts consulted in the early 1990s had unanimously recommended continuing the project.
